raw_segments.text: It was now the sweetest hour of the twenty-four, day its fervid fires had wasted, and dew
fell cool on panting plain and scorched summit, where the sun had gone down in simple state,
pure of the pomp of clouds, spread a solemn purple, burning with the light of red jewel
and furnace flame at one point, on one hill peak, and extending high and wide, soft and
The East had its own charm or fine deep blue, and its own modest gem, a rising and solitary star.
Soon it would boast the moon, but she was yet beneath the horizon.
